entities.name: Henri
entities.description: Speaker whose verbatim words open and punctuate the conversation, who calls the work a discovery of the century and later names it 'gestate'.

entities.name: The session
entities.description: The responding voice, held to the directness Henri asked for, that evaluates the discovery claim and traces the name to the vision file.

entities.name: README.md
entities.description: File in the same directory that, per this note, 'says what the set is.'

entities.name: context engineering
entities.description: One of the half-names under which many people are currently converging on the same core insight about context as the durable artifact.

entities.name: agent harnesses
entities.description: Another half-name under which the same convergence toward engineered agent environments is happening.

entities.name: card:working-standard.md
entities.description: Card already shelved in later/, waiting for the event of this feeling to be tested.

entities.name: card:project-seed.md
entities.description: Card already shelved in later/, waiting alongside working-standard for the stranger-test event.

entities.name: the stranger test
entities.description: The measure by which a claim becomes real in this method: whether properties transfer to another person, project, and model, or depend on the author being Henri.

entities.name: the environment card
entities.description: Card whose justification gained a stronger 'because' than before: not a workspace to run programs safely, but the vessel for a method there is evidence is worth carrying.

entities.name: the vision file
entities.description: Document dated 2026-08-16 that wrote 'Gestate gestates,' naming the project before Henri arrived at the same name himself.

entities.name: Gestate
entities.description: The name that now holds literally on every layer: an environment that grows programs, a tree that grows sessions, a method meant to grow music software that turned out to grow itself.

entities.name: music tool
entities.description: The original side project Henri wanted to build, out of which the tree (Gestate) emerged as a side effect.

entities.name: the review problem
entities.description: A problem faced instead of denied, cited as one of the properties that distinguishes this implementation from a mere page of instructions.

entities.name: author/session contract
entities.description: A defined contract between author and session, listed among the implementation properties not usually assembled together.

relations.description: Henri speaks his verbatim reaction and the session responds directly to it.
The session points to README.md as the document that says what the set is.
The session names context engineering as a half-name under which the same core insight is being converged on by others.
The session names agent harnesses as another such half-name.
Gestate is described as an implementation of the idea that many people converge on under the name context engineering.
This card was shelved in later/ specifically to wait for the event of the discovery feeling being tested.
This card was shelved in later/ alongside working-standard, waiting for the same event.
The card was shelved to wait for the event of applying the stranger test.
The card was likewise shelved to wait for the stranger test.
The stranger test is proposed as the measure of whether Gestate's properties transfer beyond its author Henri.
The environment card's justification is reframed around Gestate as the vessel for a method worth carrying.
Henri's naming of the project as 'gestate' turns out to have been anticipated by the vision file three days earlier.
The vision file is the source of the phrase 'Gestate gestates,' which gives the project its name.
Gestate was built alone in about ten days as a side effect of wanting to build a music tool.
Gestate is credited with facing the review problem instead of denying it, as one of its distinguishing properties.
Gestate is credited with having a defined author/session contract, one of its distinguishing properties.
